watch.description: A cedar planter box from rough boards to a finished piece in one afternoon: milling, simple box joints, a drainage gap and an oil finish that weathers well. Cut list and tool list are in the chapters below.

comments.author: @millpondmaker
comments.text: The tip about leaving a drainage gap under the bottom boards saved my last planter. Great pacing too.

comments.author: @saturdayshed
comments.text: Built two of these yesterday with offcuts. The jig for the box joints is genius.

comments.author: @fernandflint
comments.text: Which oil did you use for the finish? Mine went a bit grey after a month outside.

results.snippet: A cedar planter box from rough boards to a finished piece in one afternoon: milling, simple box joints, a drainage gap and an oil finish that weathers well.
A flea-market hand plane, rust and all, brought back to a mirror sole with sandpaper on glass, a little oil and a lot of patience.
Not woodworking at all, but the same patience: we pour water over a sand table and watch a straight channel learn to bend.
Raised beds and planter boxes dry out faster than the ground. Here is how often to water, how to tell, and why the saucer matters.
Five tents under forty, pitched side by side on a ridge in a real storm, with a hand-built wooden stake mallet for good measure.
